messages.text: Monday, September 28 · Canton, Michigan
Autumn air, a full moon rising, and local histories on display
A partly cloudy autumn day offers a high near 76°F. Local history is on display in Ypsilanti, while science explores the early assembly of our own galaxy.
Expect partly cloudy skies today with a high near 76°F and a low around 51°F.
Sunrise is at 7:28 AM, sunset at 7:20 PM, with a full moon 96.9% illuminated.
Local happenings and cultural notes

In Ypsilanti, the YDL-Superior is featuring the Ypsi Farmers & Gardeners Oral History Exhibit, offering a free look at local food growers. For music lovers, Spiral Galaxy performs at Trinosophes in Detroit at 7:30 PM.
Mark your calendar for September 30, which is My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
Ann Arbor's fiscal plans and U-M's cancer research

Ann Arbor City Council has approved a spending plan for funds from a downtown property sale, allocating $14.2 million to $17.4 million across 12 projects. The University of Michigan has also established a $10 million center to advance soundwave cancer treatments.
Tomorrow's events and learning opportunities
Tomorrow offers a fireside chat on Black Reading Month at Howard Family Bookstore in Detroit at 6 PM, and an interactive workshop on AI for everyday use at Farmington Library at 6 PM.
Space telescope finds ancient galactic collision

NASA's Hubble telescope has identified evidence of an ancient collision with a dwarf galaxy that shaped the Milky Way's early assembly. Additionally, NASA's Starling satellites have demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation in orbit.
The next Starship orbital flight attempt is estimated no earlier than September 18, 2026.
A quiet afternoon can hold a universe of discovery.
Tuesday, September 29 · Canton, Michigan
Overcast Skies Meet Autumn Air: Local Tech and Space News

Tuesday brings an overcast sky with mild temperatures, perfect for exploring local events or diving into fascinating science. NASA's Starling satellites are demonstrating new navigation techniques, a promising step for future space missions.
Expect an overcast day with a high near 76°F and a low around 50°F.
Sunrise is at 7:29 AM and sunset is at 7:19 PM, with a Waning Gibbous moon, 91.9% illuminated.
Tuesday's Local Gatherings and Talks

Consider the "AI for the Everyday: An Interactive Workshop" at the Farmington Library at 6:00 PM to explore practical AI applications. For a literary focus, the "Black Reading Month Fireside Chat" is also at 6:00 PM at Howard Family Bookstore in Detroit.
Tomorrow, September 30, marks both My Birthday and Patrick's Birthday.
State Funding Targets First Responders and Worker Health

Michigan is allocating $1.044 million to a statewide initiative for first responder mental health. Additionally, $1.3 million will support a 'three-share model' health coverage program for low-income workers.
Looking Ahead: Music and Community Events

Tomorrow, September 30, offers a "Plants and Pride" event at 11:00 AM in Livonia and "Community Table: The Washtenaw Food Hub" at 6:00 PM in Ann Arbor. The Horse Lords are playing music in Detroit at 7:30 PM.
Satellites Navigate Without GPS, Roman Telescope Cleared

NASA's Starling satellites have successfully demonstrated GPS-free autonomous navigation using onboard cameras and object catalogs. The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has also cleared its flight-readiness review and is proceeding to final launch preparations.
The next orbital Starship attempt is listed as no earlier than September 18, 2026, though this is an independent estimate and not an official SpaceX schedule.
Find a quiet corner of interest and give it your attention.
